evidence: ASK REQUIRES REAL BUILD: instruction.md:1-17 asks for a multi-user recruiting workspace in /app (Node/Express/SQLite, node /app/server.js, port 3000, DB_PATH, /api/health) with a per-job six-stage pipeline board, one-stage moves via ordinary controls, shared manual ordering, Interview capacity, optimistic move with put-back and 'who' on conflict (409 versioning, hireops_rules.md:76-87), all-or-none multi-card moves and single-use undo with conflict detection (rules:89-103), live updates within 15 s that preserve focus/drafts/open card (instruction:5, rules:119-127), paginated conversations with scroll anchoring, per-person unread, seen marks, per-user per-conversation drafts surviving reload and session expiry (rules:129-180), role permissions with 401/403/404 (rules:15-24, 68-74), a candidate portal with redaction (rules:182-200), activity log (rules:111-117), seed-once and restart durability (instruction:17). No 'trivial tweak' shape: the template instruction is 'CHANGE_ME' and the template solution is only a placeholder server, so the whole product is new work; the golden is ~1,558 lines across server.js, src/{bootstrap,db,index}.js, public/js/{app,board,threads}.js, html, css. SMALLEST-SUBMISSION ANALYSIS (quality-checks.md #7 'ask what the smallest submission satisfying the brief would be'): a static page or health-only stub is rejected by the render gate ('A static picture or only a health response is insufficient', gates/render/judge.toml:25) and the constraints gate requires a UI-added candidate, reload, and an independent Observer context seeing exactly one card ('A static seed response, a no-op success message or a browser-only save does not satisfy the gate', gates/constraints/judge.toml:51). A single CRUD screen (auth + open job + add candidate with email rules, no board/threads) can pass both gates but can earn at most hro_job_open 1 + hro_add_candidate 1 + hro_add_email_rules 1 = 3.0 of 61.0 functional weight = 0.0492, which does not exceed floors.functional = 0.05 (scoring.toml:10-11; score.py:47-48 requires scores[k] > f), so reward = 0.0. Most criteria need real board/conversation behaviour plus positive controls (e.g. hro_anonymous needs 'A signed-in success of each is the control'; hro_candidate_no_staff needs Rafael's move/multi-move/reject/undo controls; hro_restart needs messages, unread counts, activity), so a mock cannot collect them. Golden scripted observations (raw-evidence-index entry workspace.json, hash verified) show the reference actually implements the hard behaviours. LESSONS CHECK: lesson 4 (keep gates simple) holds - gates are sign-in/render and one server-backed add/readback, strictness is in scored criteria; lesson 5 nudge present (instruction.md:13); lessons 1/12 (hidden requirements, checklist-voice notes) bear on rows 1/6/27/31 rather than this row and I saw no row-7 instance (the ask is product-voiced, no build recipe beyond the template runtime contract). RISK REASONS (not a defect): (a) the stub-vs-real separation rests on a thin margin - a board-less CRUD app that also keeps an activity log of its own actions could plausibly add hro_activity/hro_activity_refusals (2 more weight -> 5/61 = 0.082 > 0.05) and then collect visual Likert credit, giving a rough analytic reward of about 0.6*0.082 + 0.2*visual(~0.5) = ~0.15; that is shaped partial credit for a genuine but partial build under the template-controlled floor, not a stub, and it is far below the golden; (b) the raw-evidence index scope states reward discrimination/ranking, full configured grading and Oracle/target scores are absent, so no measured stub/weak-app reward exists to confirm the analytic separation. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
